lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Use a live, professional code link instead of one that looks like a placeholder.
items.because: The link should go directly to work an employer should see.

items.says: Check that “Expected Jun 2026” is still accurate when applying.
Use a consistent location and date format throughout.
Say whether the 35% accuracy gain is relative or in percentage points.
items.because: The accuracy result needs enough context to be credible.

items.says: Name the baseline for the accuracy gain.
items.because: The accuracy result needs enough context to be credible.

items.says: Explain what “reviewer disagreement” measures.
items.because: Readers need to understand the comparison.

items.says: Say whether the 14% and 6% figures came from the same evaluation set.
items.because: Readers need to understand the comparison.

items.says: Identify the evaluation size or workload if space allows.
items.because: It would make the 18% and 5% gains more persuasive.

items.says: Clarify what counted as an accuracy regression.
items.because: That may not be obvious to the roles being targeted.

items.says: Remove or substantially change the repeated fine-tuning bullet.
items.because: It repeats the first bullet’s method.

items.says: The claim about learning to reproduce tool outputs may not describe what happened.
items.because: Assistant-only masking normally excludes tool outputs from the loss.

items.says: Be prepared to substantiate the attribution of the backlog reduction.
items.because: The reduction could have had other causes.

items.says: Specify what GPU memory was measured and what else changed.
items.because: Attributing a 4× reduction solely to BF16 mixed precision may prompt scrutiny.

items.says: Explain the load-test conditions.
items.because: They provide context for the latency result.

items.says: Establish whether the 420 ms and 180 ms results used comparable traffic.
items.because: The latency comparison needs to be comparable.

items.says: Fix the tense inconsistency between “maintained” and “adds”.
Clarify whether the regression checks shortened the release cycle.
items.because: Other changes may have contributed to the three-day cycle.

items.says: Add a before-and-after measure of the backlog or dispatch delay if available.
items.because: It would make the impact more concrete.

items.says: Replace or remove the broad, unmeasured adoption claim.
items.because: It does not tell readers what was built or changed.

items.says: Define what counted as working context.
items.because: The measurement behind the claim should be defensible.

items.says: Explain how the stress test was run and the 100× growth measured.
items.because: The striking 100× claim should be defensible.

items.says: Indicate how the deadlocks and lost results were verified as resolved.
items.because: A concise test or measurement would support the result.

items.says: Specify whether the contribution implemented metrics, integrated existing ones, or both.
items.because: “Integrated” alone leaves the contribution’s boundary unclear.

items.says: Clarify what was ranked for the Kendall correlation.
items.because: Readers need that to interpret the 0.89 figure.

items.says: The backlog result duplicates the Mobility Systems bullet.
The backlog result appears misplaced under the research-agent project.
items.because: It appears unrelated to the framework and could undermine trust.

items.says: Git is grouped with programming languages.
items.because: It belongs outside the programming-languages grouping.

items.says: Kubernetes is grouped with ML methods.
items.because: It belongs with infrastructure or tooling.
